newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs, pork bellies end mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs, pork bellies end mostly higher.

text.p: CME hog and pork belly futures closed mostly higher, with traders attributing much of the gain to short covering ahead of Tuesday's USDA Cold Storage Report.
The report, to be released at 1400 CST, was expected to show fewer pork bellies in storage on January 1 than a year ago.

In hogs, sources said much of the buying was short covering by individual traders. Well-financed commodity funds continued to hold onto long positions and were not active in Tuesday's session, they said.
In addition to the storage report, traders said the funds staying firm on long positions may have prompted local traders to exit their short positions.

News from the cash markets appeared bearish. Cash hogs traded mostly $1.00 to $1.50 per cwt lower in direct Midwest trade Tuesday, and it may take a week or more for producers to market hogs that were backlogged by the recent harsh weather.
"The cash news could not be worse as far as I'm concerned," said one livestock trader early in Tuesday's session.
The ample hog supply was evident in Tuesday's hog slaughter, which USDA estimated at 380,000 head. Analysts said that is near the industry's capacity.
Analysts estimated the USDA Cold Storage report may show 37.4 million to 41.5 million lbs of pork bellies in storage as of January 1 versus 30.9 million December 1 and 47.6 million a year ago.

Lean hog futures closed down 0.050 cent per lb to up 0.750 cent with February off 0.050 at 75.400 cents. Pork bellies were up 0.350 to down 0.075 cent with February up 0.250 cent at 75.300. Early in the session February traded up to 76.20.
